## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general. Alternatively, you could give that knight crest to a cavalier, who would then use it to be promoted to a paladin. The complete promotion-item mapping is below.

| item              | eligible classes → promoted class                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **hero crest**    | mercenary → hero; myrmidon → swordmaster; fighter → warrior                                          |
| **knight crest**  | cavalier → paladin; knight → general                                                                 |
| **orion's bolt**  | archer → sniper; nomad → nomad trooper                                                               |
| **elysian whip**  | pegasus knight → falcoknight; wyvern rider → wyvern lord                                             |
| **guiding ring**  | mage → sage; shaman → druid; monk → bishop; cleric → bishop; troubadour → valkyrie                   |
| **ocean seal**    | pirate → berserker                                                                                   |
| **fell contract** | thief → assassin                                                                                     |
| **earth seal**    | any class eligible for a hero crest, knight crest, orion's bolt, elysian whip, or guiding ring       |
| **heaven seal**   | lyn → blade lord; eliwood → knight lord; hector → great lord, subject to story-specific restrictions |

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- `fe7_threat` can under-claim: in Ch2 an enemy it counted as unable to reach attacked anyway. Leave a margin for wounded units. `fe7_act` `item` sometimes fails with "could not locate"; passing `item_slot` explicitly and retrying once worked.
- `fe7_act` sometimes reports "action menu could not be located" and backs out with the unit unspent (seen on rescue). Retrying the same call once works.
- `trade` hands over a whole item, and a Vulnerary is one item with 3 uses, so giving one away gives all 3 uses. When an `item`/`trade` keeps failing on one unit, give up after two tries and `wait`.
- Don't guess who a unit is from its class number. Check its inventory: a staff means a healer, a tome means a mage. Or check the portrait in a screenshot. `fe7_forecast` sometimes fails with "action menu could not be located" even after a retry; the matching `fe7_act` attack still worked straight away.
- After a chapter ends, a late Start from `fe7_wait` can leave the minimap open on the new chapter. Press B once to close it.
- Read the goal window in the opening screenshot; Ch6's was "Hit switches" (step on blue floor tiles), not seize or rout. `fe7_wait` can report story-benched units as DIED at a chapter change. Check `fe7_state`, which reports benched and fallen separately.
- Ch7 (Lyn): killing every enemy before the boss unlocked Ch7x. `fe7_forecast` sometimes says "menu could not be located" on turn 1, then works later. Before attacking a unit on a mountain or fort, forecast it — Sain swung at 26% true hit vs a mountain brigand.
- Weapon uses are running low (Lyn's Mani Katti, Rath's Short Bow, Florina's Slender Lance), and nobody has bought anything yet. Use the first armory or vendor you can reach. Enemy thieves head straight for chests and then escape, so kill or block them early.
- Shops: `fe7_act` has no `armory`/`vendor` action yet. To shop, select the unit with raw presses, move it onto the shop and pick Armory. Screenshots lag about one frame, so take two after each press. `fe7_end_turn`'s "nothing changed on the board" can be wrong: in Ch8 the enemies had advanced. Always re-read `fe7_state`/`fe7_threat`. Enemy item IDs: 0x12 Lancereaver, 0x1E Axereaver, 0x2A Swordreaver, 0x2C Iron Bow.
- A two-way `trade` swap (item_slot + take_item_slot) failed every time in Ch9. Use one-way gives and takes, through a third unit if needed. A plain `attack` swings slot 0, and a boss's equipped weapon changes after each fight, so forecast with the exact weapon every time. Kent's Armorslayer swing in Ch9 hit a Javelin and nearly got him killed.
- Against a boss whose counter could kill (Ch10 Lundgren), use hit-and-rescue. One unit attacks, a mounted ally rescues it and cantos out of range, and a dancer refreshes a tank for another swing. A dropped unit can't act that turn, so drop it a turn early. Lyn mode ends after Ch10, and answering Yes to "continue playing?" loads Eliwood's Ch11 "Taking Leave". This file has no Eliwood-mode sections.
- The run is now in **Eliwood's tale**, but `run_state.json` `mode` stays "lyn". From Ch12 on, use the Hector-mode headings, whose chapter names match. Their **Recruits** lists are Hector's, though, so check the screen for who is actually green or red. The Ch11 "Taking Leave" section was added above "## Hector mode".
- Marcus on a fort is the best tool in early Eliwood mode. Turtle with him and let the enemy suicide into his counters, but watch the uses on his Silver Lance. Ch12 and Ch13 had no prep screen and no save prompt; the chapter just rolls on.
- `fe7_act` `armory`/`vendor` are NOT implemented: the unit walks onto the shop and its turn is spent. Talk-recruit enemies like Guy, who has a Killing Edge, will kill-or-die against any unit in their range, so keep his range clear until the recruiter is adjacent.
- Shops: `fe7_act` rejects `armory`/`vendor`, but by hand it works. Select the unit (`fe7_inspect` on its tile, then A), move the cursor onto the shop, A, and pick Armory/Vendor. Then A through the text, A for Buy, pick the item, A for Yes, B B to leave. A mounted unit is left in canto afterwards: put the cursor back on it, A, then A on Wait. On a shop tile the action menu confuses `fe7_act` `item`, so step off first. Eliwood-mode chapter numbers run one lower than the Hector-mode headings (E15 "Noble Lady" is the "Chapter 16" heading here).
- `fe7_inventory_full` reports "resolved", but the game then shows a "Drop <item>? Yes/No" confirmation with **No** highlighted. Press Left, then A (and A again to clear the "Dropped" banner). A boss boxed into a gate or throne by a tank on its only entrance can't move, and dies to the tank's counters.
- `fe7_forecast` with `weapon_slot` sometimes refuses ("the weapon list had a single entry"), but the same `fe7_act attack` with `weapon_slot` works. After `fe7_inventory_full`, do NOT press A; it opens the field menu. Merlinus's tent can be attacked; at 0 HP he only retreats and returns next chapter, but guard him anyway. Eliwood cannot use the Horseslayer (it is a lance).
- `fe7_act action:'item'` (Vulnerary) only works with x,y = the unit's CURRENT tile. Using an item after a move, or after a trade in the same turn, fails ("could not put the highlight on Use"), and after a trade it leaves the unit spent. Heal first, then move next turn. Shamans (Flux) do 11-12 to Res-0 units; only Marcus (Res 9) shrugs them off. After a chapter ends, press Start one at a time with screenshots, since one press too many starts the next chapter from its prep screen.
- **Lyn's death is a Game Over in Eliwood's tale**, same as Eliwood and Hector. Treat all three as lords. Bosses that "never move" still attack anything within their weapon range on the enemy phase, and they pick soft targets. Near the top map rows `fe7_act` staff/item often fails with "menu could not be located"; do those actions by hand.
- Fog-of-war maps (Ch19): a hidden enemy can't be targeted, even adjacent, and `fe7_end_turn`'s "nothing changed on the board" missed enemy moves there, so always re-read `fe7_state`. A boss holding a bow can't counter at range 1, so check the forecast's "--" (by hand if the tool can't open the menu: A, A, read the forecast, A or B).
- Enemies whose unit flags (+0x0C) read 0x200 are invisible, can't be attacked and don't act, yet `fe7_state`/`fe7_threat` still list them (Ch21: the boss sat this way until a unit entered his area). If an attack menu shows only [item, wait] next to a listed enemy, this is why. Wyverns land on fences and roofs, so a "sealed" pocket isn't sealed against fliers. A unit's death in Eliwood's tale only ends the game for Eliwood and for Lyn **when Lyn is deployed**, and Lyn can be benched at Pick Units.
- Defend/survive chapters with a 2-wide choke: hold the tiles where the FEWEST enemy tiles can reach each holder, even if it is one row further back. Moving the line forward to recruit someone is fine for a single phase, then go back. Hector's death is a Game Over in Eliwood's tale, so keep him off the front once the monk/mage waves arrive (Res 5). `fe7_act` `item` (Elixir/Vulnerary) failed with "could not put the highlight on Use" several times this chapter; heal with Serra instead.
- Before using a unit as a blocker or bait, compare its AS with the enemy's: a gap of 4+ means it gets doubled (Heath, AS 5, died to a Spd-12 warrior in Ch23). At prep, **Trade → List** shows every unit's and the convoy's items by weapon type and lets you pull any of them. `fe7_forecast`/`fe7_act` `weapon_slot` on Marcus's lances kept being refused ("single entry"); the default weapon or a different slot worked.
- **Ballistae are invisible to the tools.** A ballista is a trap object: `fe7_terrain` shows plain and `fe7_threat` ignores it. A sniper or archer standing on one shoots at range 3-10 without its inventory uses changing. If a unit dies or loses HP with no enemy weapon use explaining it, read the attacker's BattleUnit at `0x0203A3F0` (+0x0B roster, +0x10/0x11 x,y, +0x48 u16 weapon after: item 0x34 = Ballista) and the last-acted record at `0x0202BD48`.
- Against a crit-heavy sword boss, a **Swordreaver** (axe that reverses the triangle) on a full-HP Hawkeye standing on a fort turned Lloyd's 95% hits into 29%. Look for reavers at shops before bosses. Shops: select the unit by hand, A on the shop, Buy; with a full inventory, Yes sends the item to Merlinus. Backing out without buying leaves the unit unmoved. Units next to Merlinus get a "Merch" (convoy) command that doesn't end their turn.
- Late-game survive maps flood the board with wyvern waves. Every soft unit (and the lords) should ride on a high-Def carrier (rescue); wyverns do 2-4 to Hector, Marcus, Hawkeye or Oswin. Never leave a group isolated behind mountains, because isolated groups get wiped. At prep, the Trade menu's **Use** can apply promotion items.
- Snow weather changes move costs turn to turn (horses sometimes 3 per plain), and `fe7_threat` ignores it, so use `verify` on a key enemy. A talk-recruit target that out-damages everyone (Harken) must be kept out of reach entirely; a counter crit can kill him. Range-2 attackers are free damage against bosses with a 1-range tome plus a siege tome.
- **Green NPCs can be rescued**: a carried unit can't be targeted. That's how Ch28 "Guard Zephiel" was won (Marcus carried Zephiel and Pent healed Marcus with Physic). In fog, attacking an unseen enemy makes `fe7_act` land in the Item menu with a bogus "inventory full" report: press B ×3, have another unit Wait next to the enemy first, then attack. `fe7_act staff` fails often; cast Physic by hand (A on the unit, A on the tile, Staff, Physic, Left/Right to cycle to the target, A).
- **Poison (Poison Lance) does about 3 per turn and CAN kill a 1-HP unit.** Twice in Ch29, `fe7_wait`'s A/Start presses during reinforcement-arrival events left the game on the title screen (it suspended). **Resume Chapter** returned to the same turn unchanged. A bow-only enemy (nomad, sniper) standing next to your unit can't attack it and blocks that tile for others, so it works as a "cork".
- **`fe7_threat` does not see ballistas.** A sniper sitting on a ballista tile has range 3-10, and it's effective vs fliers. Treat any enemy archer on a "Ballista" tile as covering a 10-tile radius.
- Raw-press shopping and unit selection can land on the field menu with **Suspend highlighted** if a press is dropped. Always screenshot before pressing A, and prefer retrying the `fe7_act` call, which usually works on the second try. Player slot numbers do NOT map to fixed units: check `chNN` against `overlay/names.json` (0F Louise, 15 Pent, 1A Marcus, 22 Hawkeye, 31 Florina).
- **Rescue as armour.** A unit being carried can't be targeted at all, so a Def-18 carrier that isn't doubled while carrying makes the carried unit safe. Check Spd: carrying halves it, and a carrier that gets doubled loses that edge.
- **Hidden fire traps**: some maps have invisible fire tiles that do 10 per phase. Read the trap array at `0x0203A518` (8-byte entries: x, y, type; type 4 is fire, type 2 a breakable wall with HP in byte 3). `fe7_act attack` refuses walls; attack them by hand. A chapter whose goal is "Claim a space" or "Arrive" has no Seize entry; Wait on the tile.

### Chapter 29 — Cog of Destiny

**Objectives:**

"Defeat enemy" (rout; in-game "Ch. 27: Cog of Destiny"), with a prep screen and 10 deploy slots; Merlinus deploys as a tent at (22,26). The map is 29x27 and you start in the SE (x23-28, rows 21-26). The SE pocket's only entrances are the bridges (25,18) to the north and (21,21)/(22,21) to the west, plus the (20,25) bridge from the SW. 43 enemies at the start. **Boss** (ch66, Swordmaster Lv18, 58 HP, Light Brand 1-2) sits on the throne (7,5). **Shops are in the SW corner: armory (7,26) sells Iron/Silver sword, lance, axe and bow; vendor (8,26) sells Heal, Fire, Thunder, Elfire, Lightning, Shine and Flux.** Infantry can't reach them from the east (peaks x7-9, river x10-11); Hawkeye (Berserker) can, via (12,25)->(11,25) river->(9,25) peak->(8,26). A flier would get there faster.

**Recruits:**

| character | starts as | recruit with / action | important condition                          |
| --------- | --------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| **vaida** | enemy     | **hector**            | she must have survived as an enemy in ch. 26 |

**Agent notes:**

**s29 attempt 1 (RESTARTED on turn 37 after Rebecca (t11), Nino (t19) and Oswin (t36) died).**
- Prep: sold the White Gem (Louise, 10000G at full price) and Blue Gem (Lyn, 5000G) via Trade → Sell, for 17220G total. Florina's Slim Lance went to Marcus, who had no weapon. The Heaven Seal still can't be used.
- Reinforcements: **knight waves** (1 general + 4 lance/javelin knights) at forts (14-16,10-12) on turns 4/6/8/10. **Western sword waves** (swordmaster, 2 heroes, myrmidon) at forts (6-8,14-16) on turns 16/18/20/22. **Wyvern waves** at (26-28,24-26), right next to Merlinus's tent: Vaida (ch21 Wyvern Lord, Spear 1-2, about 32 Atk, Def 21, **Res 6, so Pent's doubled Elfire kills her: keep him away**) plus 2 riders on turn 33, then **5 lance or javelin riders EVERY turn from 34**. Two nomads (longbow and short bow, Move 8) come south around turn 17.
- What worked: Hawkeye + Hector at (22,20)/(21,21) (the west bridges) and Oswin at (25,19) seal the SE pocket. Pent's Elfire behind them doubles and kills knights (Res 2-3). Knights mostly refuse to attack the walls. Hawkeye walked to the shops (turns 15-20) and bought Elfire, Heal, Silver/Iron weapons; overflow goes to Merlinus ("send to Merlinus? Yes"), and units next to the tent take it via **Merch**. Marcus with a lance on a forest killed whole sword packs on counters.
- Deaths: **Rebecca** was hit at range 2 by three javelin knights from beyond the wall (I didn't re-run threat after trades). **Nino** died to the two nomads who rode into the pocket over the open (22,21) bridge. **Oswin** died to Vaida plus riders. Merlinus's tent fell on turn 34 to the wyverns.
- **Next attempt:** deploy Florina (flier) and shop on turns 1-3; keep Rebecca and Nino out of javelin range; keep both west bridges walled the whole chapter; by turn 32 have everyone grouped with Hector, ready to Talk to Vaida, and soft units carried (rescued) by tanks before the wyverns arrive.

**s29 attempt 2 (RESTARTED on turn 9 after Oswin (t5) and Marcus (t8) died).** Prep: benched Nino and gave her Elfire to Pent; sold the gems and Hawkeye's Aura (21220G). Hawkeye left for the shops on turn 2 and bought on turns 6-7. **Sending Hawkeye west early triggered the western sword waves (swordmasters/heroes/myrmidons from forts (6-8,14-16)) from turn 3 instead of turn 16**, and they merged with the knight waves at our bridges, about 25 enemies by turn 7. The two nomads also arrived early (turn 5) and one sat on the (20,21) river tile next to the bridge. The bridge walls (Oswin unarmed, then Marcus) died to general + nomad bow + swordmaster focus. **Lesson: hold the bridges through the knight waves (turns 4-11) with Hawkeye at (22,20) and Hector at (21,21) like attempt 1, and only shop after that.** Never leave a unit under 25 HP on a wall tile.

**s29 attempt 3 (RESTARTED on turn 48 after Merlinus and Bartre died; 0 deaths until turn 46).**
- The attempt-1 wall worked again: Hector (21,21) + Hawkeye/Marcus (22,21/22,20) + Oswin (25,19), Pent behind with Elfire. Knight waves (to T11) and western sword waves (T16-T22) died on counters. Hawkeye shopped T19-T20: armory = Silver Lance x2, Silver Axe, Iron Axes, Silver Sword; vendor = Heal x2, Elfire x5 (6220G left). Pent (Sage) uses Heal staves.
- **Merch**: a unit that has NOT moved can Merch and then still move, but Merch uses up its trade. Hand items over by having the RECEIVER start the trade.
- After T22 the western enemies hold position. Lure them one at a time with Hawkeye or Marcus on tiles where `fe7_threat` shows 1. Snipers do walk forward.
- **Wyverns did NOT come on T33.** They arrived at the end of T45, right after the enemy count fell to about 10: Vaida + 2 riders, then 5 riders per turn (another run saw them stop after ~4 waves). Likely trigger: low enemy count, not turn number.
- Deaths: Merlinus (immobile tent, nobody sealed it because my army was west) and **Bartre (Spd 5: Vaida doubled him, 28x2)**. Check doubling before calling a tile survivable.

**s29 attempt 4 (GAME OVER on turn 77: Eliwood died in the enemy phase).** The restart skipped Preparations, so the default team took the field. Deaths, in order: Oswin, Louise, Pent, Rebecca, Bartre, Florina, Eliwood.

1	# Playthrough Strategy
2	
3	Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
4	its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
5	area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.
6	
7	## General Strategy
8	
9	- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.
10	
11	## Recruiting Units
12	
13	In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.
14	
15	The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.
16	
17	## Promoting Units
18	
19	Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.
20	
21	In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general. Alternatively, you could give that knight crest to a cavalier, who would then use it to be promoted to a paladin. The complete promotion-item mapping is below.
22	
23	| item              | eligible classes → promoted class                                                                    |
24	| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
25	| **hero crest**    | mercenary → hero; myrmidon → swordmaster; fighter → warrior                                          |
26	| **knight crest**  | cavalier → paladin; knight → general                                                                 |
27	| **orion's bolt**  | archer → sniper; nomad → nomad trooper                                                               |
28	| **elysian whip**  | pegasus knight → falcoknight; wyvern rider → wyvern lord                                             |
29	| **guiding ring**  | mage → sage; shaman → druid; monk → bishop; cleric → bishop; troubadour → valkyrie                   |
30	| **ocean seal**    | pirate → berserker                                                                                   |
31	| **fell contract** | thief → assassin                                                                                     |
32	| **earth seal**    | any class eligible for a hero crest, knight crest, orion's bolt, elysian whip, or guiding ring       |
33	| **heaven seal**   | lyn → blade lord; eliwood → knight lord; hector → great lord, subject to story-specific restrictions |
34	
35	## Broad strategy notes
36	
37	Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.
38	
39	- `fe7_threat` can under-claim: in Ch2 an enemy it counted as unable to reach attacked anyway. Leave a margin for wounded units. `fe7_act` `item` sometimes fails with "could not locate"; passing `item_slot` explicitly and retrying once worked.
40	- `fe7_act` sometimes reports "action menu could not be located" and backs out with the unit unspent (seen on rescue). Retrying the same call once works.
41	- `trade` hands over a whole item, and a Vulnerary is one item with 3 uses, so giving one away gives all 3 uses. When an `item`/`trade` keeps failing on one unit, give up after two tries and `wait`.
42	- Don't guess who a unit is from its class number. Check its inventory: a staff means a healer, a tome means a mage. Or check the portrait in a screenshot. `fe7_forecast` sometimes fails with "action menu could not be located" even after a retry; the matching `fe7_act` attack still worked straight away.
43	- After a chapter ends, a late Start from `fe7_wait` can leave the minimap open on the new chapter. Press B once to close it.
44	- Read the goal window in the opening screenshot; Ch6's was "Hit switches" (step on blue floor tiles), not seize or rout. `fe7_wait` can report story-benched units as DIED at a chapter change. Check `fe7_state`, which reports benched and fallen separately.
45	- Ch7 (Lyn): killing every enemy before the boss unlocked Ch7x. `fe7_forecast` sometimes says "menu could not be located" on turn 1, then works later. Before attacking a unit on a mountain or fort, forecast it — Sain swung at 26% true hit vs a mountain brigand.
46	- Weapon uses are running low (Lyn's Mani Katti, Rath's Short Bow, Florina's Slender Lance), and nobody has bought anything yet. Use the first armory or vendor you can reach. Enemy thieves head straight for chests and then escape, so kill or block them early.
47	- Shops: `fe7_act` has no `armory`/`vendor` action yet. To shop, select the unit with raw presses, move it onto the shop and pick Armory. Screenshots lag about one frame, so take two after each press. `fe7_end_turn`'s "nothing changed on the board" can be wrong: in Ch8 the enemies had advanced. Always re-read `fe7_state`/`fe7_threat`. Enemy item IDs: 0x12 Lancereaver, 0x1E Axereaver, 0x2A Swordreaver, 0x2C Iron Bow.
48	- A two-way `trade` swap (item_slot + take_item_slot) failed every time in Ch9. Use one-way gives and takes, through a third unit if needed. A plain `attack` swings slot 0, and a boss's equipped weapon changes after each fight, so forecast with the exact weapon every time. Kent's Armorslayer swing in Ch9 hit a Javelin and nearly got him killed.
49	- Against a boss whose counter could kill (Ch10 Lundgren), use hit-and-rescue. One unit attacks, a mounted ally rescues it and cantos out of range, and a dancer refreshes a tank for another swing. A dropped unit can't act that turn, so drop it a turn early. Lyn mode ends after Ch10, and answering Yes to "continue playing?" loads Eliwood's Ch11 "Taking Leave". This file has no Eliwood-mode sections.
50	- The run is now in **Eliwood's tale**, but `run_state.json` `mode` stays "lyn". From Ch12 on, use the Hector-mode headings, whose chapter names match. Their **Recruits** lists are Hector's, though, so check the screen for who is actually green or red. The Ch11 "Taking Leave" section was added above "## Hector mode".
51	- Marcus on a fort is the best tool in early Eliwood mode. Turtle with him and let the enemy suicide into his counters, but watch the uses on his Silver Lance. Ch12 and Ch13 had no prep screen and no save prompt; the chapter just rolls on.
52	- `fe7_act` `armory`/`vendor` are NOT implemented: the unit walks onto the shop and its turn is spent. Talk-recruit enemies like Guy, who has a Killing Edge, will kill-or-die against any unit in their range, so keep his range clear until the recruiter is adjacent.
53	- Shops: `fe7_act` rejects `armory`/`vendor`, but by hand it works. Select the unit (`fe7_inspect` on its tile, then A), move the cursor onto the shop, A, and pick Armory/Vendor. Then A through the text, A for Buy, pick the item, A for Yes, B B to leave. A mounted unit is left in canto afterwards: put the cursor back on it, A, then A on Wait. On a shop tile the action menu confuses `fe7_act` `item`, so step off first. Eliwood-mode chapter numbers run one lower than the Hector-mode headings (E15 "Noble Lady" is the "Chapter 16" heading here).
54	- `fe7_inventory_full` reports "resolved", but the game then shows a "Drop <item>? Yes/No" confirmation with **No** highlighted. Press Left, then A (and A again to clear the "Dropped" banner). A boss boxed into a gate or throne by a tank on its only entrance can't move, and dies to the tank's counters.
55	- `fe7_forecast` with `weapon_slot` sometimes refuses ("the weapon list had a single entry"), but the same `fe7_act attack` with `weapon_slot` works. After `fe7_inventory_full`, do NOT press A; it opens the field menu. Merlinus's tent can be attacked; at 0 HP he only retreats and returns next chapter, but guard him anyway. Eliwood cannot use the Horseslayer (it is a lance).
56	- `fe7_act action:'item'` (Vulnerary) only works with x,y = the unit's CURRENT tile. Using an item after a move, or after a trade in the same turn, fails ("could not put the highlight on Use"), and after a trade it leaves the unit spent. Heal first, then move next turn. Shamans (Flux) do 11-12 to Res-0 units; only Marcus (Res 9) shrugs them off. After a chapter ends, press Start one at a time with screenshots, since one press too many starts the next chapter from its prep screen.
57	- **Lyn's death is a Game Over in Eliwood's tale**, same as Eliwood and Hector. Treat all three as lords. Bosses that "never move" still attack anything within their weapon range on the enemy phase, and they pick soft targets. Near the top map rows `fe7_act` staff/item often fails with "menu could not be located"; do those actions by hand.
58	- Fog-of-war maps (Ch19): a hidden enemy can't be targeted, even adjacent, and `fe7_end_turn`'s "nothing changed on the board" missed enemy moves there, so always re-read `fe7_state`. A boss holding a bow can't counter at range 1, so check the forecast's "--" (by hand if the tool can't open the menu: A, A, read the forecast, A or B).
59	- Enemies whose unit flags (+0x0C) read 0x200 are invisible, can't be attacked and don't act, yet `fe7_state`/`fe7_threat` still list them (Ch21: the boss sat this way until a unit entered his area). If an attack menu shows only [item, wait] next to a listed enemy, this is why. Wyverns land on fences and roofs, so a "sealed" pocket isn't sealed against fliers. A unit's death in Eliwood's tale only ends the game for Eliwood and for Lyn **when Lyn is deployed**, and Lyn can be benched at Pick Units.
60	- Defend/survive chapters with a 2-wide choke: hold the tiles where the FEWEST enemy tiles can reach each holder, even if it is one row further back. Moving the line forward to recruit someone is fine for a single phase, then go back. Hector's death is a Game Over in Eliwood's tale, so keep him off the front once the monk/mage waves arrive (Res 5). `fe7_act` `item` (Elixir/Vulnerary) failed with "could not put the highlight on Use" several times this chapter; heal with Serra instead.
61	- Before using a unit as a blocker or bait, compare its AS with the enemy's: a gap of 4+ means it gets doubled (Heath, AS 5, died to a Spd-12 warrior in Ch23). At prep, **Trade → List** shows every unit's and the convoy's items by weapon type and lets you pull any of them. `fe7_forecast`/`fe7_act` `weapon_slot` on Marcus's lances kept being refused ("single entry"); the default weapon or a different slot worked.
62	- **Ballistae are invisible to the tools.** A ballista is a trap object: `fe7_terrain` shows plain and `fe7_threat` ignores it. A sniper or archer standing on one shoots at range 3-10 without its inventory uses changing. If a unit dies or loses HP with no enemy weapon use explaining it, read the attacker's BattleUnit at `0x0203A3F0` (+0x0B roster, +0x10/0x11 x,y, +0x48 u16 weapon after: item 0x34 = Ballista) and the last-acted record at `0x0202BD48`.
63	- Against a crit-heavy sword boss, a **Swordreaver** (axe that reverses the triangle) on a full-HP Hawkeye standing on a fort turned Lloyd's 95% hits into 29%. Look for reavers at shops before bosses. Shops: select the unit by hand, A on the shop, Buy; with a full inventory, Yes sends the item to Merlinus. Backing out without buying leaves the unit unmoved. Units next to Merlinus get a "Merch" (convoy) command that doesn't end their turn.
64	- Late-game survive maps flood the board with wyvern waves. Every soft unit (and the lords) should ride on a high-Def carrier (rescue); wyverns do 2-4 to Hector, Marcus, Hawkeye or Oswin. Never leave a group isolated behind mountains, because isolated groups get wiped. At prep, the Trade menu's **Use** can apply promotion items.
65	- Snow weather changes move costs turn to turn (horses sometimes 3 per plain), and `fe7_threat` ignores it, so use `verify` on a key enemy. A talk-recruit target that out-damages everyone (Harken) must be kept out of reach entirely; a counter crit can kill him. Range-2 attackers are free damage against bosses with a 1-range tome plus a siege tome.
66	- **Green NPCs can be rescued**: a carried unit can't be targeted. That's how Ch28 "Guard Zephiel" was won (Marcus carried Zephiel and Pent healed Marcus with Physic). In fog, attacking an unseen enemy makes `fe7_act` land in the Item menu with a bogus "inventory full" report: press B ×3, have another unit Wait next to the enemy first, then attack. `fe7_act staff` fails often; cast Physic by hand (A on the unit, A on the tile, Staff, Physic, Left/Right to cycle to the target, A).
67	- **Poison (Poison Lance) does about 3 per turn and CAN kill a 1-HP unit.** Twice in Ch29, `fe7_wait`'s A/Start presses during reinforcement-arrival events left the game on the title screen (it suspended). **Resume Chapter** returned to the same turn unchanged. A bow-only enemy (nomad, sniper) standing next to your unit can't attack it and blocks that tile for others, so it works as a "cork".
68	- **`fe7_threat` does not see ballistas.** A sniper sitting on a ballista tile has range 3-10, and it's effective vs fliers. Treat any enemy archer on a "Ballista" tile as covering a 10-tile radius.
69	- Raw-press shopping and unit selection can land on the field menu with **Suspend highlighted** if a press is dropped. Always screenshot before pressing A, and prefer retrying the `fe7_act` call, which usually works on the second try. Player slot numbers do NOT map to fixed units: check `chNN` against `overlay/names.json` (0F Louise, 15 Pent, 1A Marcus, 22 Hawkeye, 31 Florina).
70	- **Rescue as armour.** A unit being carried can't be targeted at all, so a Def-18 carrier that isn't doubled while carrying makes the carried unit safe. Check Spd: carrying halves it, and a carrier that gets doubled loses that edge.
71	- **Hidden fire traps**: some maps have invisible fire tiles that do 10 per phase. Read the trap array at `0x0203A518` (8-byte entries: x, y, type; type 4 is fire, type 2 a breakable wall with HP in byte 3). `fe7_act attack` refuses walls; attack them by hand. A chapter whose goal is "Claim a space" or "Arrive" has no Seize entry; Wait on the tile.
72	
73	### Chapter 29 — Cog of Destiny
74	
75	**Objectives:**
76	
77	"Defeat enemy" (rout; in-game "Ch. 27: Cog of Destiny"), with a prep screen and 10 deploy slots; Merlinus deploys as a tent at (22,26). The map is 29x27 and you start in the SE (x23-28, rows 21-26). The SE pocket's only entrances are the bridges (25,18) to the north and (21,21)/(22,21) to the west, plus the (20,25) bridge from the SW. 43 enemies at the start. **Boss** (ch66, Swordmaster Lv18, 58 HP, Light Brand 1-2) sits on the throne (7,5). **Shops are in the SW corner: armory (7,26) sells Iron/Silver sword, lance, axe and bow; vendor (8,26) sells Heal, Fire, Thunder, Elfire, Lightning, Shine and Flux.** Infantry can't reach them from the east (peaks x7-9, river x10-11); Hawkeye (Berserker) can, via (12,25)->(11,25) river->(9,25) peak->(8,26). A flier would get there faster.
78	
79	**Recruits:**
80	
81	| character | starts as | recruit with / action | important condition                          |
82	| --------- | --------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
83	| **vaida** | enemy     | **hector**            | she must have survived as an enemy in ch. 26 |
84	
85	**Agent notes:**
86	
87	**s29 attempt 1 (RESTARTED on turn 37 after Rebecca (t11), Nino (t19) and Oswin (t36) died).**
88	- Prep: sold the White Gem (Louise, 10000G at full price) and Blue Gem (Lyn, 5000G) via Trade → Sell, for 17220G total. Florina's Slim Lance went to Marcus, who had no weapon. The Heaven Seal still can't be used.
89	- Reinforcements: **knight waves** (1 general + 4 lance/javelin knights) at forts (14-16,10-12) on turns 4/6/8/10. **Western sword waves** (swordmaster, 2 heroes, myrmidon) at forts (6-8,14-16) on turns 16/18/20/22. **Wyvern waves** at (26-28,24-26), right next to Merlinus's tent: Vaida (ch21 Wyvern Lord, Spear 1-2, about 32 Atk, Def 21, **Res 6, so Pent's doubled Elfire kills her: keep him away**) plus 2 riders on turn 33, then **5 lance or javelin riders EVERY turn from 34**. Two nomads (longbow and short bow, Move 8) come south around turn 17.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general. Alternatively, you could give that knight crest to a cavalier, who would then use it to be promoted to a paladin. The complete promotion-item mapping is below.

| item              | eligible classes → promoted class                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **hero crest**    | mercenary → hero; myrmidon → swordmaster; fighter → warrior                                          |
| **knight crest**  | cavalier → paladin; knight → general                                                                 |
| **orion's bolt**  | archer → sniper; nomad → nomad trooper                                                               |
| **elysian whip**  | pegasus knight → falcoknight; wyvern rider → wyvern lord                                             |
| **guiding ring**  | mage → sage; shaman → druid; monk → bishop; cleric → bishop; troubadour → valkyrie                   |
| **ocean seal**    | pirate → berserker                                                                                   |
| **fell contract** | thief → assassin                                                                                     |
| **earth seal**    | any class eligible for a hero crest, knight crest, orion's bolt, elysian whip, or guiding ring       |
| **heaven seal**   | lyn → blade lord; eliwood → knight lord; hector → great lord, subject to story-specific restrictions |

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- `fe7_threat` can under-claim: in Ch2 an enemy it counted as unable to reach attacked anyway. Leave a margin for wounded units. `fe7_act` `item` sometimes fails with "could not locate"; passing `item_slot` explicitly and retrying once worked.
- `fe7_act` sometimes reports "action menu could not be located" and backs out with the unit unspent (seen on rescue). Retrying the same call once works.
- `trade` hands over a whole item, and a Vulnerary is one item with 3 uses, so giving one away gives all 3 uses. When an `item`/`trade` keeps failing on one unit, give up after two tries and `wait`.
- Don't guess who a unit is from its class number. Check its inventory: a staff means a healer, a tome means a mage. Or check the portrait in a screenshot. `fe7_forecast` sometimes fails with "action menu could not be located" even after a retry; the matching `fe7_act` attack still worked straight away.
- After a chapter ends, a late Start from `fe7_wait` can leave the minimap open on the new chapter. Press B once to close it.
- Read the goal window in the opening screenshot; Ch6's was "Hit switches" (step on blue floor tiles), not seize or rout. `fe7_wait` can report story-benched units as DIED at a chapter change. Check `fe7_state`, which reports benched and fallen separately.
- Ch7 (Lyn): killing every enemy before the boss unlocked Ch7x. `fe7_forecast` sometimes says "menu could not be located" on turn 1, then works later. Before attacking a unit on a mountain or fort, forecast it — Sain swung at 26% true hit vs a mountain brigand.
- Weapon uses are running low (Lyn's Mani Katti, Rath's Short Bow, Florina's Slender Lance), and nobody has bought anything yet. Use the first armory or vendor you can reach. Enemy thieves head straight for chests and then escape, so kill or block them early.
- Shops: `fe7_act` has no `armory`/`vendor` action yet. To shop, select the unit with raw presses, move it onto the shop and pick Armory. Screenshots lag about one frame, so take two after each press. `fe7_end_turn`'s "nothing changed on the board" can be wrong: in Ch8 the enemies had advanced. Always re-read `fe7_state`/`fe7_threat`. Enemy item IDs: 0x12 Lancereaver, 0x1E Axereaver, 0x2A Swordreaver, 0x2C Iron Bow.
- A two-way `trade` swap (item_slot + take_item_slot) failed every time in Ch9. Use one-way gives and takes, through a third unit if needed. A plain `attack` swings slot 0, and a boss's equipped weapon changes after each fight, so forecast with the exact weapon every time. Kent's Armorslayer swing in Ch9 hit a Javelin and nearly got him killed.
- Against a boss whose counter could kill (Ch10 Lundgren), use hit-and-rescue. One unit attacks, a mounted ally rescues it and cantos out of range, and a dancer refreshes a tank for another swing. A dropped unit can't act that turn, so drop it a turn early. Lyn mode ends after Ch10, and answering Yes to "continue playing?" loads Eliwood's Ch11 "Taking Leave". This file has no Eliwood-mode sections.
- The run is now in **Eliwood's tale**, but `run_state.json` `mode` stays "lyn". From Ch12 on, use the Hector-mode headings, whose chapter names match. Their **Recruits** lists are Hector's, though, so check the screen for who is actually green or red. The Ch11 "Taking Leave" section was added above "## Hector mode".
- Marcus on a fort is the best tool in early Eliwood mode. Turtle with him and let the enemy suicide into his counters, but watch the uses on his Silver Lance. Ch12 and Ch13 had no prep screen and no save prompt; the chapter just rolls on.
- `fe7_act` `armory`/`vendor` are NOT implemented: the unit walks onto the shop and its turn is spent. Talk-recruit enemies like Guy, who has a Killing Edge, will kill-or-die against any unit in their range, so keep his range clear until the recruiter is adjacent.
- Shops: `fe7_act` rejects `armory`/`vendor`, but by hand it works. Select the unit (`fe7_inspect` on its tile, then A), move the cursor onto the shop, A, and pick Armory/Vendor. Then A through the text, A for Buy, pick the item, A for Yes, B B to leave. A mounted unit is left in canto afterwards: put the cursor back on it, A, then A on Wait. On a shop tile the action menu confuses `fe7_act` `item`, so step off first. Eliwood-mode chapter numbers run one lower than the Hector-mode headings (E15 "Noble Lady" is the "Chapter 16" heading here).
- `fe7_inventory_full` reports "resolved", but the game then shows a "Drop <item>? Yes/No" confirmation with **No** highlighted. Press Left, then A (and A again to clear the "Dropped" banner). A boss boxed into a gate or throne by a tank on its only entrance can't move, and dies to the tank's counters.
- `fe7_forecast` with `weapon_slot` sometimes refuses ("the weapon list had a single entry"), but the same `fe7_act attack` with `weapon_slot` works. After `fe7_inventory_full`, do NOT press A; it opens the field menu. Merlinus's tent can be attacked; at 0 HP he only retreats and returns next chapter, but guard him anyway. Eliwood cannot use the Horseslayer (it is a lance).
- `fe7_act action:'item'` (Vulnerary) only works with x,y = the unit's CURRENT tile. Using an item after a move, or after a trade in the same turn, fails ("could not put the highlight on Use"), and after a trade it leaves the unit spent. Heal first, then move next turn. Shamans (Flux) do 11-12 to Res-0 units; only Marcus (Res 9) shrugs them off. After a chapter ends, press Start one at a time with screenshots, since one press too many starts the next chapter from its prep screen.
- **Lyn's death is a Game Over in Eliwood's tale**, same as Eliwood and Hector. Treat all three as lords. Bosses that "never move" still attack anything within their weapon range on the enemy phase, and they pick soft targets. Near the top map rows `fe7_act` staff/item often fails with "menu could not be located"; do those actions by hand.
- Fog-of-war maps (Ch19): a hidden enemy can't be targeted, even adjacent, and `fe7_end_turn`'s "nothing changed on the board" missed enemy moves there, so always re-read `fe7_state`. A boss holding a bow can't counter at range 1, so check the forecast's "--" (by hand if the tool can't open the menu: A, A, read the forecast, A or B).
- Enemies whose unit flags (+0x0C) read 0x200 are invisible, can't be attacked and don't act, yet `fe7_state`/`fe7_threat` still list them (Ch21: the boss sat this way until a unit entered his area). If an attack menu shows only [item, wait] next to a listed enemy, this is why. Wyverns land on fences and roofs, so a "sealed" pocket isn't sealed against fliers. A unit's death in Eliwood's tale only ends the game for Eliwood and for Lyn **when Lyn is deployed**, and Lyn can be benched at Pick Units.
- Defend/survive chapters with a 2-wide choke: hold the tiles where the FEWEST enemy tiles can reach each holder, even if it is one row further back. Moving the line forward to recruit someone is fine for a single phase, then go back. Hector's death is a Game Over in Eliwood's tale, so keep him off the front once the monk/mage waves arrive (Res 5). `fe7_act` `item` (Elixir/Vulnerary) failed with "could not put the highlight on Use" several times this chapter; heal with Serra instead.
- Before using a unit as a blocker or bait, compare its AS with the enemy's: a gap of 4+ means it gets doubled (Heath, AS 5, died to a Spd-12 warrior in Ch23). At prep, **Trade → List** shows every unit's and the convoy's items by weapon type and lets you pull any of them. `fe7_forecast`/`fe7_act` `weapon_slot` on Marcus's lances kept being refused ("single entry"); the default weapon or a different slot worked.
- **Ballistae are invisible to the tools.** A ballista is a trap object: `fe7_terrain` shows plain and `fe7_threat` ignores it. A sniper or archer standing on one shoots at range 3-10 without its inventory uses changing. If a unit dies or loses HP with no enemy weapon use explaining it, read the attacker's BattleUnit at `0x0203A3F0` (+0x0B roster, +0x10/0x11 x,y, +0x48 u16 weapon after: item 0x34 = Ballista) and the last-acted record at `0x0202BD48`.
- Against a crit-heavy sword boss, a **Swordreaver** (axe that reverses the triangle) on a full-HP Hawkeye standing on a fort turned Lloyd's 95% hits into 29%. Look for reavers at shops before bosses. Shops: select the unit by hand, A on the shop, Buy; with a full inventory, Yes sends the item to Merlinus. Backing out without buying leaves the unit unmoved. Units next to Merlinus get a "Merch" (convoy) command that doesn't end their turn.
- Late-game survive maps flood the board with wyvern waves. Every soft unit (and the lords) should ride on a high-Def carrier (rescue); wyverns do 2-4 to Hector, Marcus, Hawkeye or Oswin. Never leave a group isolated behind mountains, because isolated groups get wiped. At prep, the Trade menu's **Use** can apply promotion items.
- Snow weather changes move costs turn to turn (horses sometimes 3 per plain), and `fe7_threat` ignores it, so use `verify` on a key enemy. A talk-recruit target that out-damages everyone (Harken) must be kept out of reach entirely; a counter crit can kill him. Range-2 attackers are free damage against bosses with a 1-range tome plus a siege tome.
- **Green NPCs can be rescued**: a carried unit can't be targeted. That's how Ch28 "Guard Zephiel" was won (Marcus carried Zephiel and Pent healed Marcus with Physic). In fog, attacking an unseen enemy makes `fe7_act` land in the Item menu with a bogus "inventory full" report: press B ×3, have another unit Wait next to the enemy first, then attack. `fe7_act staff` fails often; cast Physic by hand (A on the unit, A on the tile, Staff, Physic, Left/Right to cycle to the target, A).
- **Poison (Poison Lance) does about 3 per turn and CAN kill a 1-HP unit.** Twice in Ch29, `fe7_wait`'s A/Start presses during reinforcement-arrival events left the game on the title screen (it suspended). **Resume Chapter** returned to the same turn unchanged. A bow-only enemy (nomad, sniper) standing next to your unit can't attack it and blocks that tile for others, so it works as a "cork".
- **`fe7_threat` does not see ballistas.** A sniper sitting on a ballista tile has range 3-10, and it's effective vs fliers. Treat any enemy archer on a "Ballista" tile as covering a 10-tile radius.
- Raw-press shopping and unit selection can land on the field menu with **Suspend highlighted** if a press is dropped. Always screenshot before pressing A, and prefer retrying the `fe7_act` call, which usually works on the second try. Player slot numbers do NOT map to fixed units: check `chNN` against `overlay/names.json` (0F Louise, 15 Pent, 1A Marcus, 22 Hawkeye, 31 Florina).
- **Rescue as armour.** A unit being carried can't be targeted at all, so a Def-18 carrier that isn't doubled while carrying makes the carried unit safe. Check Spd: carrying halves it, and a carrier that gets doubled loses that edge.
- **Hidden fire traps**: some maps have invisible fire tiles that do 10 per phase. Read the trap array at `0x0203A518` (8-byte entries: x, y, type; type 4 is fire, type 2 a breakable wall with HP in byte 3). `fe7_act attack` refuses walls; attack them by hand. A chapter whose goal is "Claim a space" or "Arrive" has no Seize entry; Wait on the tile.

The SE pocket's only entrances are the bridges (25,18) to the north and (21,21)/(22,21) to the west, plus the (20,25) bridge from the SW. 43 enemies at the start. **Boss** (ch66, Swordmaster Lv18, 58 HP, Light Brand 1-2) sits on the throne (7,5). **Shops are in the SW corner: armory (7,26) sells Iron/Silver sword, lance, axe and bow; vendor (8,26) sells Heal, Fire, Thunder, Elfire, Lightning, Shine and Flux.** Infantry can't reach them from the east (peaks x7-9, river x10-11); Hawkeye (Berserker) can, via (12,25)->(11,25) river->(9,25) peak->(8,26). ### Chapter 31 — Sands of Time

**Objectives:**

"Protect throne": survive 11 turns (the win fired as turn 12 began) without an enemy reaching the throne at (6,2). Map 22x28. The throne room (x0-12, rows 0-4) opens ONLY through two stairways: west (1-2, rows 5-7) and east (10-12, rows 5-7). A separate walled side room (x13-18, rows 11-16) holds four forced-deployed units (Pent, Canas, Wil, Hawkeye). It opens via the one-wide stairs (14,14) and the 2-wide east strip x17-18. Enemies: Poison Lance knights (Mt 4, harmless), archers, longbows (range 3, they shoot through walls), Flux/Luna shamans, druids with Sleep/Silence staves and Eclipse (3-10), thieves (they loot the chests at (3,12), (4,12) and (3,23)), and Generals. Reinforcements arrive every turn from the south edge and the NE stairs (15,2)/(20,2).

**Recruits:**

None.

**Agent notes:**

**s12: WON on attempt 1 (survived to turn 12). Wil DIED (EP7: he was asleep in the side room, and two longbow shots through the wall plus a knight finished him). No recruits.**
- What worked: Hector sat on the throne all chapter and was never touched. Seal both throne-room stairways: west Oswin (2,5) + Isadora (1,5) (only 1-2 enemies ever came); east Harken (10,5)/(10,6), Marcus (11,5), Louise (12,4). Each turn Marcus speared whatever archer/shaman stepped into (12,5) and Louise shot the one on (12,6) at range 2. About 20 enemies died on counters.
- The side room is the weak point. The druid at the south put Wil and Hawkeye to SLEEP and SILENCED Canas on EP3. Longbows hit 3 tiles through walls, so row 11-12 tiles are not safe from the hall. Next time kill the druid on turn 2-3 with Pent, and keep everyone in (14,13) (stairs top), (16,13) and (17,13). Hawkeye rescuing an 8-HP Canas kept him alive.
- Prep: benched Guy and Bartre (unarmed). Nils, Nino, Kent, Vaida and Matthew are unarmed or unavailable. Tomahawk (Marcus) and Iron Axe (Hector) went to Hawkeye; Marcus's spare Silver Lance went to Oswin. Isadora and Sain CANNOT use Silver Lances (greyed out); Sain still holds one and has no usable weapon.
- Handover: WEAPONS ARE NEARLY GONE. Louise Silver Bow x2, Marcus Silver Lance x5, Oswin Silver Lance x3, Harken Silver Sword about x1 + Light Brand x1, Hawkeye Tomahawk x4 + Iron Axe x37, Pent Elfire about x9, Canas Flux x12 + Heal x23. Hector has Steel Sword x6, Silver Axe x16, Wolf Beil x30. Isadora holds the Heaven Seal and Marcus the Elysian Whip; Florina holds a Red Gem and Thunder. Gold was 19,077, and the 31x intro gives +30,000.
- Ending: Save screen. The cursor started on the Ch.15 slot (!). I moved it Up to the slot in use ("Ch.31: Sands of Time", play time 19:42) and saved. Ch.31x loaded. An extra Start skipped its Prep and answered "Deploy Merlinus?" (Yes, the default). The handover is at **Ch.31x TURN 1**, player phase, 10 units deployed, objective "Get supplies 1/5 Turn", no enemies. Buy weapons there.

### Chapter 31x — Battle Preparations (gaiden)

**Objectives:**

"Get supplies": a 5-turn town with no enemies; the chapter ends after turn 5. Map 15x10. Armories at (10,2), (13,2), (7,3), (10,8); Vendors at (1,4), (12,5); Arena (5,7); House (13,8). Gold at start of T1: 49,077.

**Recruits:**

| character | starts as | recruit with / action | important condition                                                                                              |
| --------- | --------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **karla** | npc       | **bartre**            | bartre must be a **level 5+ warrior**, be deployed, talk to her, and both must survive their forced combat round |

**Agent notes:**

**s13: WON on attempt 1 (the chapter ends by itself after turn 5). No deaths. Karla NOT recruited: s12's extra Start skipped this chapter's Prep, so Bartre was never deployed and Karla never showed up.**
- Shops: (13,2) axes (Iron/Steel/Silver/Killer/Swordreaver/Hand axe), (10,2) lances (Slim/Iron/Steel/Silver/Killer/Axereaver/Javelin), (7,3) swords (Slim/Iron/Steel/Silver/Killing Edge/Lancereaver), (10,8) bows (Iron/Steel/Silver/Killer/Short/Long?). (1,4) tomes (Fire/Thunder/Elfire/Lightning/Shine/Divine/Flux), (12,5) items (Vulnerary/Elixir 3000/Pure Water/Door Key/Heal/Mend/Recover/Restore). There is NO convoy here ("no merchant"), so a unit with 5 items cannot buy. Sell junk first. Shopping is all by hand; fe7_act has no armory/vendor action in this build. Mounted units canto after a shop, so press A on a tile, then Wait.
- Gold: 49,077 -> sold Red Gem 2,500, White Gem 10,000 and a spare Heaven Seal 10,000 -> spent to **26,232 left**. The shop list cursor remembers its last row, so press Up to the top before counting Downs (I bought a Restore by accident and sold it back).
- **Lyn PROMOTED to Blade Lord** (Heaven Seal; item 0x89).
- Purchases now held: Lyn Silver Lance x2 + Silver Sword. Eliwood Silver Lance x3 + Killer Lance. Canas Silver Sword x2 + Killing Edge. Hector Silver Sword (HE CANNOT USE IT, rank too low) + Killing Edge. Marcus Hand Axe, Killer Axe, Silver Axe, Elixir and the Elysian Whip (for Florina). Louise Silver Bow x3 + Killer Bow x2. Rath Silver Bow. Isadora Elfire x3 + Mend. Oswin Thunder (and Divine x25, for a light user if there is one). Hawkeye Elixir x3.
- **At Ch.32 Prep, redistribute**: fresh Silver Lances to Marcus/Oswin/Kent/Vaida; Hector's Killer/Hand Axe from Marcus; Elfire to Pent/Nino; Silver Swords to Harken/Guy/Lyn; Mend to Pent or Canas. Old Silver Lance x3 (Oswin) and Steel Sword x6 (Hector) are nearly spent.
- Ending: no save prompt after 31x. At Ch.32 Prep I used Prep > Save on the slot in use (it read "Ch.31x: Battle Preparations", play time 20:29), so Restart Chapter now lands on Ch.32. The handover is at the **Ch.32 Prep screen** ("Seize gate"), with 16 units auto-deployed and 32 enemies. The boss (ch85, cls5A, 68 HP) is at (24,3).

content.text:
I won Chapter 31 (Sands of Time) on the second attempt: the "protect the throne" timer ran out and the chapter ended as turn 12 began. Nobody died, and there was no one to recruit. The game is now on the Preparations screen of the next chapter, the 31x gaiden (in-game "Ch. 29x: Battle Preparations", objective "Get supplies").

**Attempt 1 was a Game Over on turn 4.** A druid's Berserk staff, which reaches about 17 tiles, turned Hawkeye and then Marcus against us. Berserked allies act on their own as soon as my last unit moves, and they attack lords. The two of them killed Lyn. My hiding spot failed because I wrongly treated a pillar as a wall; pillars are passable.

**Attempt 2 worked like this:**
- **Fewer units:** I deployed only Eliwood, Hector, Lyn, Pent, Marcus and Hawkeye. Lyn used the Heaven Seal and is now a Blade Lord, and Eliwood took Pent's Rapier.
- **Lords carried all chapter:** carried units can't be targeted by attacks, staves or berserked allies. Hawkeye carried Lyn, and Hector took Eliwood onto the throne partway through. Hector held the throne with my units, or enemy archers that can't shoot point-blank, on the tiles beside it.
- **Defusing the Berserk druid:** it stays put until someone comes within its reach, so I kept everyone outside it for the first three enemy phases. When it finally cast, it hit Pent, who was holding only a Heal staff, so it did no harm.
- **Keeping the carriers alive:** Pure Water went on Hector and Hawkeye. I passed Elixirs to the boxed-in Hawkeye by trading them hand to hand, and Pent healed Marcus every turn.

**Things the next session needs to know:**
- **Save slot 3 was overwritten.** During the ending, the waiting tool's button presses saved the result into slot 3, replacing the old "Ch. 16" save. I then saved again into slot 1, the slot in use, so both now read "Ch. 29x: Battle Preparations".
- **Pent's Elfire disappeared** during an enemy phase. I couldn't tell how, and he now has only a Heal staff. Weapons are thin all round, so the shops in 31x matter.
- Hawkeye, Marcus and Pent were still poisoned at the end.
- Karla can't be recruited in 31x because Bartre is dead.

Files are in `playthroughs/2026-10-20_00-09/`:
- **Save state:** `states/s36_ch31_sands-of-time.ss`

- **CURRENT_RUN_STRATEGY.md:** the Chapter 31 section is filled in, plus two cross-chapter notes on Berserk and the save slot.
